name: Manako
title: Pinned: Most AI still automates tasks. The next shift is AI that can run business operations. The progression looks a lot like autonomous driving. Just as cars moved from driver assistance to partial, conditional, and higher autonomy, business operations will move through the same stages: 0. Manual operations → people observe, decide and act. 1. Assisted operations → AI detects events. People act. (This is where Vision Agents sit today.) 2. Partial automation → AI executes tasks. People supervise. 3. Conditional autonomy → AI runs workflows. People handle exceptions. 4. High autonomy → AI runs a defined operation, including its exceptions. 5. Autonomous operations — AI coordinates and improves end-to-end operations. The long-term direction is clear: increasing operational autonomy. People set the goals, the policies and the accountability. AI runs more of the operations. Humans govern. At Manako Labs, we’re building World Models for Business so this progression can actually happen in the physical world, starting with the cameras companies already have. Vision Agents are the entry point. Levels 2–5 are the ambition.

name: SemiAnalysis
title: ASML is bringing lithography-grade precision to hybrid bonding. “BESI, ASMPT and others come from a pick-and-place background. They’re very good at overlaying each die onto the base wafer and placing it down. The bond itself forms later, during the anneal.” “ASML is coming at it from the front end. Its tools already do sub-nanometer overlay for lithography, easily an order of magnitude more precise. And as hybrid bond pitches get finer, how many signals you can fit per square millimeter between two dies matters more and more.” “Overlay isn’t ASML’s problem. The challenge is building a system that brings the dies to the wafer, or in this case, the wafer to the die.”

name: Jon Durbin
title: There are ~two economies: attention and revenue. Focus on whichever you like but if you only pick one, it probably eventually breaks. Free high intelligence = maximum attention (but probably financial/resource crisis), and conversely maximally expensive commodities restricting access rugs the attention eventually and likewise probably leads to collapse. Parallax and the new "living model" type system created out of it is perhaps a way to foster both by decreasing prices (run on phone, macbook, spark, whatever) rather than increasing them further (with larger and larger models), and ideally maintaining the intelligence (and boosting creativity/customization via this epigenesis project to prevent too much concentration into any single company/model). Ideally, everyone just brings their own resources to fund the training (sparks + apple + amd) then they own the output forever and can shape it any which way with baking in their own memory/knowledge/rules into the otherwise sparse weights after training.
